title: Paper
text:
Gannon, J Andrés. “A Text-as-Data Approach to Measuring Interstate Relations Using National Security Strategies.” Working paper.
Abstract: How states regard one another – which states command attention, and with what evaluative orientation – is central to international relations, yet it is measured with proxies that are largely binary, symmetric, and slow-moving because they are built for other purposes. I develop and validate a text-as-data method that recovers directed dyad-year indices of a state’s expressed salience (prominence) and affinity (evaluative stance) toward other states from its national security strategy. The method automates the judgments a careful reader would make – which states a government names, how prominently, and in what evaluative terms – and makes them consistently across hundreds of documents. Applied to a new public corpus of 438 national security strategy documents issued by 92 countries (1962–2024) – to date the most comprehensive cross-national, multi-decade collection of security-strategy texts – the approach produces continuous, directional, and time-varying measures of interstate posture. Because governments revise these documents every few years rather than every few decades, the measures register shifts in stated posture as they happen, an early signal alongside slower-moving indicators such as UN votes and alliances. The measures converge with benchmarks such as alliance portfolio similarity and UN voting patterns where they should, track human judgments of expressed orientation, and diverge from the benchmarks where expressed and behavioral alignment part ways. In application, the scores add incremental predictive validity for militarized interstate dispute onset and diplomatic visits beyond these benchmarks, and reveal an asymmetry – cooperation tracks both a target’s prominence and its warmth, while conflict tracks prominence most strongly, with expressed hostility contributing a smaller association. The corpus, processing code, and derived measures are publicly released, providing a replicable tool for extracting conveyed relationships from political texts.










Pre-print (November 2026)











GitHub repo (forthcoming)





The paper analyzes a subset of this website’s catalog: English-language documents from the core corpus, with the selection rules described in the paper. The Data page lists every catalogued document.

title: Changelog
text:
2026.11

Corpus synchronized with the project’s master document inventory; text and chunked-text files are now named exactly as in the metadata, which fixes links that previously failed for 36 documents.
Added New Zealand’s 2000 Government Defence Policy, Argentina’s 2018 National Defence Policy, and the English-language edition of Croatia’s 2018 Strategic Defence Review.
Re-extracted text for Taiwan 2008, Bulgaria 2010, and Denmark 2010 to repair spacing and extraction errors.
Removed text files that did not correspond to a catalogued document.
New: one searchable table for all documents with per-document PDF, TXT, and CSV links; bulk zip downloads of all texts and all chunked texts; downloads of any search or filter result (metadata, texts, or chunked texts); a codebook; this changelog.
The headline document count now covers the full catalog, including documents outside the core corpus.

title: Codebook
text: One record is one document: a national security strategy, defense white paper, military doctrine, or related strategy document issued by a government (or the European Union) in a given year. The catalog currently holds 823 documents, of which 586 form the core corpus (see keep below).

title: Codebook
text: One record is one document: a national security strategy, defense white paper, military doctrine, or related strategy document issued by a government (or the European Union) in a given year. The catalog currently holds 823 documents, of which 586 form the core corpus (see keep below).

title: Codebook
text:
File naming
Every file shares a stem built from the metadata:
{country_name}_{year}_{TitleWithoutSpaces}[_noneng]
The _noneng suffix marks documents not written in English. The same stem names the PDF (.pdf), the full text (.txt), and the chunked text (_chunks.csv), so the three versions of a document can always be matched.

title: Codebook
text:
Metadata (nss_metadata.csv)







Variable
Description




file_names
Name of the original PDF; the stem links it to the text files.


country_name
Issuing country, lowercase with spaces removed (e.g. southkorea, us, eu).


year
Year of publication.


title
Document title (English translation for non-English documents).


language
eng for English-language documents, noneng otherwise.


keep
1 = core corpus: whole-of-government national security and defense strategy documents. 0 = catalogued but outside that scope, such as sectoral strategies (cyber, counterterrorism), corporate and investment plans, foreign-policy white papers, and duplicate editions. Both are available for download.


type
Issue-specific strategies: cyber or terrorism; blank for general strategy documents.

title: Codebook
text:
Full text (.txt)
Text extracted from the PDF and saved as Markdown-flavored plain text. Documents with clean digital text were extracted with pymupdf4llm; scanned or difficult documents were processed with the OCR-based Marker pipeline. The text keeps headings, tables, and page furniture as extracted, so it can contain OCR errors, image placeholders such as ![](...), and running headers. Non-English documents are provided in their original language.

title: Codebook
text:
Chunked text (_chunks.csv)
Each document’s text split into chunks of at most about 128 tokens within Markdown sections, for text-as-data work. Text is lowercased.







Variable
Description




chunk_id
Position of the chunk within the document, starting at 1.


text
Chunk text.


char_length, word_count, token_count
Length of the chunk in characters, words, and model tokens.


section_index
Index of the document section the chunk belongs to.


source_file
Text file the chunk was built from.


processed_date
When the chunk was produced.

title: Codebook
text:
All texts in one table
The single-file download holds page-level text for every document, with columns doc_text, doc_type, doc_number (page), doc_name (file stem), year, country, cow_code, and cow_alpha (Correlates of War country codes).

title: Military Doctrines Dataset
text:
The Military Doctrines dataset is a catalog of 823 national security strategies, defense white papers, and related strategy documents issued by 112 countries, territories, and organizations from 1962 to 2025. The documents are collected from government websites and other online repositories in their original PDF format and converted into machine-readable text and chunked CSV formats. All three versions can be browsed and downloaded; the codebook documents the files and variables, and the changelog records what changed in each release.
The Military Doctrines project is led by J Andrés Gannon, Assistant Professor of Political Science at Vanderbilt University.
